why: A (universes 0; riemEMetricSpace, riemMetricSpace definitions): ‖q − p‖ ≤ ρ(p, q) for ANY subset N ⊆ V (chord bound, ambient); ρ = riemDist continuous on N × N (ℝ≥0∞-valued, N possibly disconnected); ρ < ∞ on a preconnected N; and the metric space riemMetricSpace hN hconn has the topology of N (definitionally, by replaceTopology). B: for every abstract connected Hausdorff Riemannian manifold: any two points are joined by a piecewise smooth path, the real ρ is a metric, it induces the topology, and it is continuous on M × M. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: A lives in an ambient inner-product space; abstract Riemannian manifolds are not of that form, so A cannot be applied (B is true and believed provable outright from Mathlib's riemannianEDist theory plus path dictionaries, ~hundreds of lines, not attempted, and it would not use A). B ⇒ A fails on content: B has nothing about the ambient V (chord bound) and only covers connected manifolds (A's continuity also covers disconnected N); arbitrary slice models Z are also beyond the bridge. Embedded special case: on ↥N (Z = ℝⁿ, N connected), A's first three conjuncts imply all of B's conclusion, and B's conclusion implies A's second and third conjuncts.
